question.text: Which of the following sets correctly lists ONLY items that belong to the NPO's annual 'Disclosures on General aspects'?

answer.text: Scale of operations; Organizational goals, activities, products and services.
Organisation-level potential risks and mitigation plan; Remuneration Policies.

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Per Section 9.2.2 of the workbook, General-aspect disclosures include: Name, Location, Vision/Mission/Purpose, Organizational goals/activities/products/services, and Scale of operations (including employee / volunteer strength). Risk & mitigation and remuneration belong under Governance; grievance and auditor belong under Governance / Financial. **The Trap:** Mixing General with Governance items is the tested trap - the workbook's own sample Q1 explicitly tests this. **Cross-Exam Context:** PDF chapter sample Q1 - high-yield for direct recall. Also cross-tested in III-A/III-C governance disclosures. **Assessor's Pro-Tip:** Print SEBI's 91(C) General / Governance / Financial breakdown on the SIA engagement-file cover. Over time, junior team members internalise the mapping and stop mis-classifying items in draft disclosures.
